body:
_This review was posted by an AI agent (OpenHands)._

Thanks for adding the `/changelog` page — the design is clean, the reuse of existing `page-wrap`/`page-title`/`detail-block` styling is appropriate, the nav link addition in `lib/garage-content.ts` is well placed, and the test coverage in `tests/changelog.test.ts` is thoughtful (empty-updates case, same-day tie-breaking, missing/blank author fallback, ISO-timestamp truncation, and live-registry ordering).

However, I found a critical correctness bug in `lib/changelog.ts` that breaks the feature and the test suite as currently written at this commit (`e8ef4c3d228ccd97c917fba9e2ad411217bc0b6f`):

- `buildChangelogEntries` sorts entries newest-first and then calls `.slice(1)`, which unconditionally discards the single newest entry from the combined feed (see inline comment). This means the `/changelog` page will never show the most recent update across the entire registry, and if the feed only has one entry it renders as if there were zero updates.
- I ran the test suite at this commit and confirmed it fails: `npx vitest run` → **4 failed / 82 passed / 1 skipped (87 total)**, not the 87/87 the PR description claims. The failing tests are exactly the ones that would catch this bug: "combines updates from every agent into one feed, newest first", "orders same-day updates by agent name", and both "shows 'unknown' when an update's author is missing/blank" tests (the latter two throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'author')` because `entries[0]` is `undefined` after the erroneous slice).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` passes cleanly, so this is purely a logic/runtime bug, not a type issue.

This needs to be fixed before merge — removing the trailing `.slice(1)` should restore the intended newest-first ordering and make the existing tests pass again.

🔄 CHANGES REQUESTED

_inline_comments.body_summary: Bug: newest changelog entry is silently dropped — .slice(1) removes the first element after the newest-first sort
